"Rude" was named after the reggae term "[[rude boy]]" and originally based on a real-life situation. The lead singer of Magic!, [[Nasri (musician)|Nasri]], had been in an unhealthy relationship with a previous girlfriend. After the two of them got into a fight with each other, the band based the song off that headline. sections.heading: Critical reception
sections.wikitext: Critical reviews for "Rude" have been mixed. [[4Music]] complimented the song, saying: "One listen and you'll be hooked."<ref name="4music">{{cite episode|title=This Week's Fresh Music Top 20|network=[[4Music]]|airdate=25 July 2014}}</ref> An article in ''[[Psychology Today]]'' drew a connection between the lyrics of the song and social attitudes about [[interracial relationships]],<ref name="race">{{cite web|url=http://www.psychologytoday.com/blog/intersections/201401/why-you-gotta-be-so-rude-i-m-gonna-marry-her-anyway|title=Why You Gotta Be So Rude? I'm Gonna Marry Her Anyway | publisher=Psychology Today | author=Kyle D Killian Ph.D. | date=January 17, 2014 | access-date=February 20, 2015}}</ref> while ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]'' magazine named "Rude" the worst song of 2014, criticizing its "sanitized reggae-fusion sound" and lyrics.<ref>{{cite magazine |url=http://time.com/3613505/top-10-worst-songs/ |title=Top 10 Worst Songs |magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]] |publisher=[[Time Inc.]] |date=December 2, 2014 |access-date=December 11, 2014 |archive-date=December 18, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141218035417/http://time.com/3613505/top-10-worst-songs/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> [[Renowned for Sound]] gave "Rude" a 4 out of 5 star rating, calling the track "lighthearted fun."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://renownedforsound.com/index.php/single-review-magic-rude/|title=Single Review: Magic! - 'Rude'|work=Renowned for Sound|last=Ryan|first=Ben|date=November 13, 2013|access-date=June 17, 2018}}</ref>
sections.text: Critical reviews for "Rude" have been mixed. 4Music complimented the song, saying: "One listen and you'll be hooked." An article in Psychology Today drew a connection between the lyrics of the song and social attitudes about interracial relationships, while Time magazine named "Rude" the worst song of 2014, criticizing its "sanitized reggae-fusion sound" and lyrics. Renowned for Sound gave "Rude" a 4 out of 5 star rating, calling the track "lighthearted fun."

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext: The music video was filmed in November 2013, directed by David Rousseau.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=27X0J-cIFtQ | title=MAGIC! - Rude (Behind the Scenes) | website=[[YouTube]] | date=June 17, 2014 }}</ref> It features the band singing the song in a garage while scenes show Nasri in a relationship with a woman played by model Ayla Parker. After this, Nasri asks her conservative father, played by actor Brian Knudson,<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.brianknudson.com/resume/ | title=Resume | publisher=Brian Knudson | access-date=February 20, 2015 | archive-date=January 10, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150110065329/http://www.brianknudson.com/resume/ | url-status=dead }}</ref> for her hand in marriage, but the father refuses and won't explain why. The mother, played by actress Mary Kay McCartney, is somewhat softer. Eventually, Nasri secretly proposes to her and together with the rest of the band, try to convince the father, but he still refuses. Nasri marries her anyway and all party in the garage as Parker proclaims her love for Nasri and she abandons her overprotective father's house once and for all. The video was released on the band's YouTube account on December 5, 2013.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PIh2xe4jnpk | title=MAGIC! - Rude | publisher=ournameismagicVEVO | date=December 5, 2013 | access-date=February 20, 2015}}</ref> As of December 2024, the video has over 2.5 billion views on [[YouTube]], and is one of the top 70 most viewed videos on the site.<ref>{{cite web|title=Top 1000 Most Viewed YouTube Videos of All Time|url=https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PL11E57E1166929B60 |publisher=YouTube|access-date=March 27, 2020}}</ref>
sections.text: The music video was filmed in November 2013, directed by David Rousseau. It features the band singing the song in a garage while scenes show Nasri in a relationship with a woman played by model Ayla Parker. After this, Nasri asks her conservative father, played by actor Brian Knudson, for her hand in marriage, but the father refuses and won't explain why. The mother, played by actress Mary Kay McCartney, is somewhat softer. Eventually, Nasri secretly proposes to her and together with the rest of the band, try to convince the father, but he still refuses. Nasri marries her anyway and all party in the garage as Parker proclaims her love for Nasri and she abandons her overprotective father's house once and for all. The video was released on the band's YouTube account on December 5, 2013. As of December 2024, the video has over 2.5 billion views on YouTube, and is one of the top 70 most viewed videos on the site.

sections.text:
On December 9, 2013, the band made their Australian television debut on Sunrise, where they performed "Rude". In June 2014, the band performed an acoustic version of the song on On Air with Ryan Seacrest. In July, they performed it on The View and on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon. On August 10, 2014, the band performed the song at the 2014 Teen Choice Awards. Magic! and American singer Marc Anthony performed a Spanglish version of the song at the 15th Latin Grammy Awards ceremony in 2014 with Anthony singing parts of the song in Spanish.

In September 2014, 15ECONDS (now Aviwkila) performed the song on Rising Star Indonesia. Their performance got a 94% approval rating from viewers.

On July 15, 2015, Postmodern Jukebox released a cover version of the song on YouTube, featuring Von Smith.

In September 2015, American singer Selena Gomez covered the song on BBC Radio 1's Live Lounge.

sections.heading: Chart performance
sections.wikitext:
"Rude" entered the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] at number 97 on May 10, 2014.<ref name="USdebut">{{cite magazine|url=http://www.billboard.com/charts/hot-100?page=9 |title=The Hot 100 |page=10 |magazine=Billboard |date=May 10, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140328101115/http://www.billboard.com/charts/hot-100?page=9 |archive-date=March 28, 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On the issue dated July 26, 2014, the song reached number one, marking their first and only number-one single. "Rude" spent six consecutive weeks at number one. On the chart issue dated September 6, 2014, the song tumbled from number one to number 5 on the Hot 100 as [[Taylor Swift]]'s "[[Shake It Off]]" debuted atop the chart. This is the first time since [[Black Eyed Peas|The Black Eyed Peas]]' "I Gotta Feeling" that a song fell all the way to the number 5 spot after spending as many as six weeks atop the chart. The song spent 16 weeks in the chart's top 10. Magic! is the sixth Canadian band to top the ''Billboard'' Hot 100, the first since [[Nickelback]] with "[[How You Remind Me]]" in 2001. It is also the ninth reggae song to reach the summit, the last being [[Sean Paul]]'s "[[Get Busy]]" in 2003.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Trust|first1=Gary|title=Magic!'s 'Rude' Tops Hot 100; Iggy Azalea's 'Fancy' Falls to No. 2|url=https://www.billboard.com/pro/magic-rude-hot-100-iggy-azalea-fancy-sam-smith-disclosure-latch/|publisher=Billboard|access-date=16 July 2014}}</ref>

"Rude" reached number two on the [[Digital Songs|''Billboard'' Hot Digital Songs]] on June 18, 2014, selling 207,000 digital copies.<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Keith|last=Caulfield|title=Jack White's 'Lazaretto' Debuts at No. 1, Sets Vinyl Sales Record|url=http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/6121606/jack-whites-lazaretto-debuts-at-no-1-sets-vinyl-sales-record|magazine=Billboard|publisher=Prometheus Global Media|date=2014-06-18|access-date=2014-06-18}}</ref> The following week the song peaked at number one, selling 210,000. It is only the second reggae song to top the ''Billboard'' Hot Digital Songs, after [[Sean Kingston]]'s "[[Beautiful Girls (Sean Kingston song)|Beautiful Girls]]" in 2007.<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Gary|last=Trust|title=Iggy Azalea Leads Hot 100 For Fifth Week, Maroon 5 Debuts In Top 20|url=http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/6133923/hot-100-iggy-azalea-maroon-5-fancy-maps|magazine=Billboard|publisher=Prometheus Global Media|date=2014-06-25|access-date=2014-07-01}}</ref> The song was certified three-times Platinum by the RIAA in September 2014 and has sold 3 million copies in the US, as of January 2015.<ref name="sales">{{cite web|url=https://www.yahoo.com/music/mark-ronson-bruno-mars-jump-to-1-on-hot-100-107450414521.html |title=Mark Ronson, Bruno Mars Jump to #1 on Hot 100 |last=Grein |first=Paul |date=January 7, 2015 |access-date=January 7, 2015 }}</ref>

"Rude" peaked at number six on the [[Canadian Hot 100]] and remained on the chart for 69 weeks. In Australia, "Rude" peaked at number two on the [[Australian Singles Chart]]. In New Zealand, the song peaked at number two on the [[New Zealand Singles Chart]]. In the United Kingdom, "Rude" debuted at number 50 on the [[UK Singles Chart]] on July 20, 2014 ― for the week ending date July 26, 2014 ― before climbing to number two a week later. The song topped the chart on August 3, 2014 ― for the week ending date August 9, 2014 ― becoming Magic!'s first chart-topper in Britain. The song peaked at number two in Ireland.
sections.text:
"Rude" entered the US Billboard Hot 100 at number 97 on May 10, 2014. On the issue dated July 26, 2014, the song reached number one, marking their first and only number-one single. "Rude" spent six consecutive weeks at number one. On the chart issue dated September 6, 2014, the song tumbled from number one to number 5 on the Hot 100 as Taylor Swift's "Shake It Off" debuted atop the chart. This is the first time since The Black Eyed Peas' "I Gotta Feeling" that a song fell all the way to the number 5 spot after spending as many as six weeks atop the chart. The song spent 16 weeks in the chart's top 10. Magic! is the sixth Canadian band to top the Billboard Hot 100, the first since Nickelback with "How You Remind Me" in 2001. It is also the ninth reggae song to reach the summit, the last being Sean Paul's "Get Busy" in 2003.

"Rude" reached number two on the Billboard Hot Digital Songs on June 18, 2014, selling 207,000 digital copies. The following week the song peaked at number one, selling 210,000. It is only the second reggae song to top the Billboard Hot Digital Songs, after Sean Kingston's "Beautiful Girls" in 2007. The song was certified three-times Platinum by the RIAA in September 2014 and has sold 3 million copies in the US, as of January 2015.

"Rude" peaked at number six on the Canadian Hot 100 and remained on the chart for 69 weeks. In Australia, "Rude" peaked at number two on the Australian Singles Chart. In New Zealand, the song peaked at number two on the New Zealand Singles Chart. In the United Kingdom, "Rude" debuted at number 50 on the UK Singles Chart on July 20, 2014 ― for the week ending date July 26, 2014 ― before climbing to number two a week later. The song topped the chart on August 3, 2014 ― for the week ending date August 9, 2014 ― becoming Magic!'s first chart-topper in Britain. The song peaked at number two in Ireland.
